clue.text: Temporary measure to fix 12?

parts.note: 12 across means on one occasion, so this is a makeshift repair meant to do the job just this one time

explanation.surface: Someone asks what stopgap would mend the thing in clue 12.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift, improvised repair is exactly a stopgap fix rigged up for temporary use.

clue.text: Bird devouring cut banger

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing, so the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: the jay is a crow-family bird
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A bird gobbles up a chopped sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a sausage (British slang) but is slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a dilapidated old car, which is exactly a jalopy.

clue.text: Still an answer

definitions.meaning: a still is distilling apparatus, and a glass flask with a long bent neck is used for this

explanation.surface: Nonetheless a reply comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is both a laboratory distilling vessel and a quick, sharp reply.

clue.text: Top host

parts.note: the top is the big top, a circus tent, and the person presiding over the show there

explanation.surface: Praise for the best entertainer of guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The circus master of ceremonies introduces acts under the big top, hosting the show.

clue.text: Start off eating chops with big fellow

indicators.note: chops as in chops and changes, so the remaining letters are rearranged
start off says the first letter of the next word is removed

explanation.surface: A large man begins tucking into lamb chops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' takes E from EATING, leaving ATING, which 'chops' rearranges. 'chops' looks like meat but is the anagram signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant is a person of great size, a big fellow.

clue.text: Embellishment would be loud if not new

indicators.note: the clue says the answer would be the word for loud if it lacked the new letter, so that letter sits inside it

parts.note: loud colours are garish, gaudy and showy

explanation.surface: A decoration that would be too gaudy were it not fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take the answer, remove N (new) and you get GARISH (loud); so N goes inside GARISH. 'would be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a decorative addition, especially to food, so it is an embellishment.

clue.text: Clap for American turn and not South American bird

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go
nor means and not
the rhea is a large flightless bird of South America

explanation.surface: Applause for an American, turning on a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clap' is slang for the disease; 'for American' because this is the US spelling (British has GONORRHOEA).
explanation.definitionFit: The clap is a slang name for this sexually transmitted infection, spelt here the American way.

clue.text: Impetuous openers to run after second hit

indicators.note: openers are the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hit, as in baseball scoring

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman's openers dash for a run after another boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen, here the first letters of 'run' and 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting without thought of consequences, which is impetuous.

clue.text: State complaint with one never-ending racket

parts.note: an ill is an ailment or complaint
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: never-ending says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: racket means noise, a din

explanation.surface: Someone moans of an ailment and a din that won't stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts NOISE to NOIS; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Midwestern US state, home to Chicago.

clue.text: Dither about fey treatment for allergic reaction

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: to haver is to dither or vacillate

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a whimsical cure for allergies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dither' is the Scottish verb meaning to vacillate; 'treatment' signals the anagram, 'about' the enclosure, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the allergic response to pollen, causing sneezing and streaming eyes.

clue.text: It's spoken retrospectively by some in Italy?

indicators.note: retrospectively says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A language once spoken in Italy, looking back over history.
explanation.definitionFit: A language is something spoken, and this one was the tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Target someone who is relatively friendly?

definitions.meaning: a figure set up at fairs to have things thrown at it, hence anyone made an easy object of attack
read playfully as a relative (an aunt) who is sociable, like a pal

explanation.surface: A target turns out to be a kindly relation.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally was a fairground dummy pelted with balls, so the phrase means an easy target of criticism.

clue.text: Urgent for every English representative on the right

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
a Tory is a Conservative, politically on the right

explanation.surface: An English MP on the right wing insists everything is pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A peremptory demand is one insisting on immediate attention, so it is urgent and allowing no refusal.

clue.text: Head beheaded on one occasion

indicators.note: beheaded says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A head is chopped off at a single event.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is informal British for the head; removing its first letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means a single time, i.e. on just one occasion in the past.

clue.text: Study studies consumed by dew, say

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
dens are studies, private rooms for work
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Learning that research gets swallowed up by morning dew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' looks like a container indicator but supplies ATE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is an example of water formed by condensation, so it is a condensate.

clue.text: Shy censor in scramble to concur in time

indicators.note: scramble says the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A timid censor gets into a muddle trying to keep pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder: SHY + CENSOR + IN, eleven letters, rearranged by 'scramble'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make things happen at the same moment is to make them coincide or concur in time.

clue.text: Shelter shimmering in sunset gets hot inside

indicators.note: inside says that letter is placed within the rearranged letters
shimmering suggests the letters waver and move into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A shelter glowing in the sunset becomes warm within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shimmering' is the anagram signal, 'inside' the insertion, 'gets' a link. This shelter is a semicircular corrugated-iron hut used in both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The corrugated-iron hut was used as quick military accommodation, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: Send letter for total

definitions.meaning: to dash off and post a letter
to total a car is to wreck it beyond repair

explanation.surface: Post a letter for the full amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to dash off and send a letter and to wreck a vehicle completely, as an insurer would.

clue.text: Allow cracking way to follow game

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a route is a way
let means allow

explanation.surface: Permission to break through a path leading to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a casino gambling game with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: State announced pedestrian security measure?

indicators.note: announced says the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a road island is a raised refuge in mid-street where people on foot can wait safely

explanation.surface: A state's name is heard as a safety refuge for walkers.
explanation.walkthrough: A traffic or road island lets pedestrians cross a busy street in two stages.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest US state, in New England, is one of the fifty states of the union.

clue.text: Face up to adversity or, perhaps, to heat in kitchen

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Cope with hardship, or else, as the saying goes, put up with kitchen heat.
explanation.walkthrough: TO HEAT IN KITCHEN has fifteen letters, rearranged by 'perhaps'; 'or' is a link. The surface recalls 'if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from boxing, means to accept a blow or misfortune bravely, facing up to adversity.

clue.text: "Given some buffets" — weightwatchers' slogan?

definitions.meaning: read as three words, a slimmer's motto: be size ten

explanation.surface: Being offered some spreads clashes with a dieting motto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffets' are blows, not spreads of food; read as BE A TEN, a UK dress size, the second sense becomes a slimmer's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten means struck repeatedly, which is what buffeting does.

clue.text: Settled back with time and inclination

indicators.note: back says the word for settled is read in reverse

parts.note: lit as in a bird that lit on a branch, i.e. settled or alighted

explanation.surface: Someone sat back, taking their time and their preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LIT into TIL; 'with' joins on T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is a slope or lean, so it is an inclination.

clue.text: Centre-page spread is cut

indicators.note: spread says the letters are laid out differently, jumbled

explanation.surface: A centrefold layout in a magazine gets trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut is informal for one's share of the takings, a proportion or slice of the total.

clue.text: Nothing's caught by rod from boat

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a cane is a rod
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty catch from a fishing rod on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Drug giving rise to male member

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A narcotic that excites a man of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp, the cannabis plant, is a source of the drug.

clue.text: See 19
Turn away from right way when other way round

indicators.note: the clue lists right before way, and this phrase says to put them in the reverse order

parts.note: Ave, short for avenue, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone told to turn off the correct road and head the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert one's eyes is to turn them away, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Able to admit jump's dive

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: fit as in fit to work, i.e. capable or able
a leap is a jump

explanation.surface: Someone capable of taking a plunge into the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEAPIT is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a seedy establishment, and a fleapit is such a grubby picture house.

clue.text: Team always getting 100

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A side that always scores a century.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Premier League football club in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an English football club, so an example of a team.
